subject: Primelane: sudden throughput starvation + latency surge
messages:
From: Alex Murray <alex.murray@primelane.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@primelane.com>, Primelane SRE <sre@primelane.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Primelane production: requests failing / massive tail latency

Marissa / David —

We started seeing a huge throughput drop and sustained 5xx + 1–3s tail latency on our /v1/generate endpoint around 08:45 PDT. Traffic is within our reserved commit but requests are queuing and then timing out. This is impacting our checkout flows; we have customers dropping out.

I attached the short logs from our side. Can you confirm whether this maps to any dedicated GPU pool saturation on your end? We need an ETA for mitigation — if you cannot restore steady throughput we will have to consider fallback to a different provider during this window.

Priya (SRE) is monitoring error rates and can share traces. Please escalate — this needs exec attention if not resolved within the hour.

— Alex
Alex Murray
Head of Engineering, Primelane
https://primelane.com

Attachments: primelane_latency_log_0914.txt
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murray <alex.murray@primelane.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@primelane.com>
Cc: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Primelane production: requests failing / massive tail latency

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’m escalating to Ops + Eng. Initial read from our telemetry: we see sustained queue depth increase in the us-west dedicated pool serving Primelane and a concurrent KV-cache miss storm from recent prompt diversity. I’ve looped David and Rishi to confirm whether we hit headroom limits or if there’s an ongoing noisy neighbor.

Immediate asks:
- David / Rishi: can you snapshot the Primelane pool (headroom, GPU utilization, queued tokens) and confirm whether autoscale/burst failed to open?
- Alex / Priya: can you confirm if you cut over any large prompt sets or changed model variant in the last 12 hours?

We will propose a short-lived fallback (smaller context model variant + aggressive batching) that preserves correctness if we cannot restore capacity in 30–45m. I’ll send an exec note if it looks like we need a contractual burst or credit to cover emergency burst capacity.

— Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Murray <alex.murray@primelane.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@primelane.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Primelane production: requests failing / massive tail latency

Quick snapshot from the pool (us-west-prime-dedicated-12):
- Average GPU utilization: 98–100% on 6/8 nodes
- Queue depth: 2.8k requests (90th pct token queueing > 1.6s)
- Autoscale events: 3 attempts since 08:50 — two aborted due to quota gate, one succeeded but added only 1 node (delayed by provisioning).
- Error spike: 5xx rate up to 11% from 0.3% baseline

Root cause hypothesis: concurrent increase in burst traffic from another tenant in the same pool plus increased per-request token cost (larger prompts) triggered KV-cache eviction churn, which killed the expected per-token throughput. Our autoscaler attempted to spin capacity but hit a soft quota guard tied to the customer's reserved slice.

Immediate mitigations applied by ops:
- Isolated Primelane’s reserved slots to prioritize their queued requests (soft routing) — lowered noisy-neighbor interference.
- Dropped nonessential background model warmups.
- Enabled emergency prefix-KV cache retention for Primelane's recent sessions (reduces repeated recompute).

Effect so far: tail latency reduced from ~1.8–2.4s to ~0.9–1.2s; 5xx down to 4.5% and trending down. We still see throughput below their committed QPS by ~18%.

Next: request exec approval for one-hour burst to add two extra GPUs to the dedicated pool and temporarily lift the quota guard for Primelane. Marissa — can you confirm commercial sign-off or permission to auto-commit emergency burst (we will track for credit/offset)?

— David
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Murray <alex.murray@primelane.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@primelane.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Primelane production: requests failing / massive tail latency

Thanks — technical addendum and suggested rollback plan.

Findings:
- KV-cache churn is the dominant inefficiency: their prompt set diversity (confirmed by Priya) caused repeated cache misses, inflating CPU->GPU transfer and per-token compute.
- Noisy neighbor contributed ~30% of extra queue time; isolation reduced it.
- Model variant compatibility: Primelane is on model-redwood-xl-13B-int8; we can fallback to model-redwood-xl-7B-int4 without functional regressions for 65% of their call patterns (we matched against their evaluation set).

Suggested steps (priority order):
1) Approve 1-hour emergency burst (2 GPUs) while we stabilize.
2) Switch Primelane traffic to 7B-int4 for non-critical endpoints and lower context windows where acceptable (rolling canary).
3) Apply stricter routing policies to prevent other tenants from scaling into Primelane's reserved slices for 2 hours.
4) Post-incident: propose prompt-caching rules and a lightweight guidance doc for Primelane on prompt templates to reduce cache churn.

If we get the burst approved now we can meet committed throughput within ~12–18m and fully restore SLOs within the hour.

— Rishi
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Murray <alex.murray@primelane.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@primelane.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Primelane production: requests failing / massive tail latency

Summary & exec ask: we partially mitigated and reduced errors/latency but throughput remains ~12–18% below commit. Ops and Eng recommend a one-hour emergency burst (+2 GPUs) and temporary routing isolation; Eng also recommends a canary fallback to 7B-int4 for non-critical endpoints.

Commercial note: Primelane has a reserved commitment but we need an explicit short-term approval for emergency burst capacity that would be billed as 'burst remuneration' and reconciled in the MA plan. I have a draft MA (attached) with proposed credits if we cannot fully meet SLO within 24h.

Requested approvals:
- Naomi (Head of Revenue): authorize offering Primelane emergency burst coverage and sign off on the credit proposal in the MA draft.
- Irene (Chief Product/Platform): authorize temporary quota lift for the two GPUs and confirm no policy/regulatory blockers.
- David/Rishi: proceed with the burst and canary fallback once approvals are in and notify Primelane immediately.

Alex/Priya — thank you for patience. We'll proceed on internal approvals and update you in the next 20 minutes.

— Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
